title: Resolving classes make denominator pro-diagrams essentially constant
statement: Let C and H be categories, W a morphism property on C with right calculus of fractions and two-out-of-three [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], F:C→H a functor, and P a class of objects. Suppose every X admits s:X'→X in W with X' in P, and F inverts every W-arrow between objects of P. Then for each X the denominator diagram G:W/X→H is essentially constant [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram]. More precisely, there exist Y and a cone u:Y→G with a stage j₀ and retraction r:G(j₀)→Y satisfying u(j₀)r=id and the common-stage factorization criterion of essential constancy. If X is in P, the leg u(id_X) is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the right Ore square from LeftFraction.exists_rightFraction to construct common predecessors in W/X. Use HasRightCalculusOfFractions.ext to construct equalizers. The identity denominator gives nonemptiness; hence W/X is cofiltered.

Let R be the full subcategory of denominators whose source lies in P. Resolve the source of any denominator to obtain an arrow from R. Mathlib initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered_of_fullyFaithful proves its inclusion initial; of_exists_of_isCofiltered_of_fullyFaithful also proves R cofiltered. Two-out-of-three and hinv make every map in the restricted F-diagram invertible. Mathlib EventuallyConstant supplies its limit cone, normalized to have identity leg at a chosen r₀. Extend this cone along the initial inclusion; the extended leg at r₀ remains the identity.

For any denominator j choose a common predecessor of r₀ and j, then resolve its source again. The transition a to r₀ lies between resolving objects and is inverted by F. Cone naturality and the identity leg imply u(k)F(a)=id; invertibility gives u(k)=F(a)⁻¹. Naturality at b then gives F(b)=F(a)u(j), the required factorization with retraction r=id. This explicitly verifies IsEssentiallyConstantProDiagram.

If X lies in P, its identity denominator is an object of R. Because every restricted transition is invertible, EventuallyConstant.isIso_π_of_isLimit makes the corresponding restricted cone leg invertible. extendCone_obj_π_app at the identity morphism identifies the extended leg with that restricted leg.

theorem resolvingClass_essentialConstancy
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {H : Type uH} [Category.{vH} H]
    (W : MorphismProperty C) [W.HasRightCalculusOfFractions]
    [W.HasTwoOutOfThreeProperty] (F : C ⥤ H) (P : Set C)
    (hres : ∀ X : C, ∃ (X' : C) (s : X' ⟶ X), X' ∈ P ∧ W s)
    (hinv : ∀ (X X' : C) (s : X ⟶ X'),
      X ∈ P → X' ∈ P → W s → IsIso (F.map s)) (X : C) :
    let G := MorphismProperty.Over.forget W ⊤ X ⋙ Over.forget X ⋙ F
    ∃ (Y : H) (u : (Functor.const (W.Over ⊤ X)).obj Y ⟶ G),
      IsEssentiallyConstantProDiagram G Y ∧
        (∃ (j₀ : W.Over ⊤ X) (r : G.obj j₀ ⟶ Y),
          u.app j₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 Y ∧
            ∀ j : W.Over ⊤ X, ∃ (k : W.Over ⊤ X) (a : k ⟶ j₀) (b : k ⟶ j),
              G.map b = G.map a ≫ r ≫ u.app j) ∧
        ∀ h : W (𝟙 X), X ∈ P →
          IsIso (u.app (⟨Over.mk (𝟙 X), h⟩ : W.Over ⊤ X))
